purpose: Running count of the Phase 2 reserve slices a study has spent. The pre-registration in verification/phase2-data-preregistration.json is a frozen snapshot of the data step and is never back-edited; this file changes instead.
rule: A study spends the reserve slice named after it, at most once. A second entry for the same slice means the slice was observed twice and its guarantee is void.

entries.note: Two non-iterated passes, one per surface, scoring one ensemble each. The pre-registered scope was the arm selected on validation plus the no-augmentation control; validation selected the control itself, so they coincided. Both surfaces are now burned for the published no-augmentation N1 ensemble.

reassigned_from_its_named_study.why_the_slice_was_free: P-1's pre-registered design states 'Test-evaluation budget: zero' and 'existing splits, no reserve groups consumed' (PLAN-PROPOSAL.md section 5, P-1). P-1 ran and closed on 2026-07-31 with verdict 'fail' (verification/p1-ensemble-spread.json) without reading this archive, so the slice its name reserved was never going to be spent by it.
reassigned_from_its_named_study.what_this_costs: P-1 can never be re-run against an unobserved synthetic surface using this slice. That is accepted: P-1 is closed, and its refutation was decided on validation by construction.
reassigned_from_its_named_study.rule_note: The ledger rule is one entry per slice, at most once. This is that one entry for p1; the slice is now burned for every purpose, not only for this one.

entries.note: One non-iterated pass per arm, four in total, no grid and no re-optimisation. Nothing was trained and no learned-lane test evaluation was spent: all four arms are classical engines. The slice is now burned and no later study may quote it.

One non-iterated pass per configuration. Both configurations were fixed before the slice was read: 0.06 is the shipped value and 0.12 was selected on the validation split, which no classical constant sweep had used. The slice is now burned for C3 flooding depth.
